title: Deploy ASP.NET Core to App Service
description: Create an App Service plan and deploy an ASP.NET Core app using Visual Studio and the Azure CLI.

data.text: You can deploy ASP.NET Core to App Service directly from Visual Studio, through GitHub Actions, or with the Azure CLI. This lesson shows the first two approaches.
Create the App Service Plan and Web App
You can create the infrastructure from Visual Studio or with the Azure CLI. The CLI is useful for scripts and automation.

data.title: Create an App Service plan and web app with Azure CLI
data.content: Run these commands in PowerShell or Bash.
data.code:
$resourceGroup = "azure-for-aspnet-rg"
$planName = "azure-for-aspnet-plan"
$webAppName = "azure-for-aspnet-demo"

az appservice plan create \
  --name $planName \
  --resource-group $resourceGroup \
  --sku B1 \
  --location eastus

az webapp create \
  --name $webAppName \
  --resource-group $resourceGroup \
  --plan $planName \
  --runtime "DOTNETCORE|8.0"

items: Right-click the ASP.NET Core project and choose **Publish**
Choose the existing resource group and web app, or create a new one

data.text: Deploy with .NET Publish and Zip Deploy
You can also publish a self-contained or framework-dependent deployment package and push it with curl or PowerShell.

data.title: Publish and deploy with Zip Deploy
data.content: Zip Deploy is useful for CI/CD pipelines and scripted deployments.
data.code:
dotnet publish -c Release -o ./publish
Compress-Archive -Path ./publish/* -DestinationPath ./publish.zip

$publishUrl = "https://azure-for-aspnet-demo.scm.azurewebsites.net/api/zipdeploy"
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $publishUrl -Method POST -InFile ./publish.zip -Credential (Get-Credential)

data.title: Deploy a sample API
data.description: Publish a minimal API to App Service and verify the response.
steps: Create a minimal API with `dotnet new web -n WeatherApi`
Add a GET `/weather` endpoint returning a JSON forecast
Deploy with Zip Deploy or Visual Studio Publish
data.expectedOutcome: You see the weather JSON response served from Azure App Service.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use Visual Studio Publish for manual deployments
Use Zip Deploy or GitHub Actions for automated deployments
App Service runs the published output without IIS management
Store connection strings in Application Settings, not in code
data.takeaway: Deployment is the moment your local ASP.NET Core app becomes a live Azure endpoint.
